subject: Physics
standard_explanation: Geometric optics explores the rectilinear propagation, reflection, and refraction of light waves. The Law of Reflection specifies that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection (θi = θr). Refraction describes the bending of light at the interface between media of differing optical densities, governed by Snell's Law (n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂). Convex lenses converge incident parallel rays to a real focus (positive focal length), while concave lenses diverge rays outward.
simplified_explanation: Light loves to travel in straight laser lines! When light hits a shiny mirror, BOUNCE! It bounces straight back (Reflection), like throwing a rubber ball against a wall. When light enters clear glass or water, it slows down and gently bends (Refraction). A curved magnifying glass (Convex Lens) bends sunlight together to a tiny bright point!
key_points: Reflection: Light bounces off smooth shiny surfaces like mirrors (Angle in = Angle out).
Refraction: Light bends when passing from air into water or glass because its speed changes.
Convex Lens (bulging outwards): Converges light rays together to a sharp focal point.
Concave Lens (curving inwards): Spreads light rays apart outwards.
A rainbow forms because raindrops refract and separate sunlight into 7 colors!
examples: Looking in your bathroom mirror in the morning shows reflection.
A pencil in a glass of water looking bent or broken at the surface shows refraction.
Magnifying glasses and eyeglasses using curved lenses to help us read clearly.
misconceptions: Misconception: Light bends because it gets tired. Fact: Light bends because it travels slower in dense glass or water than in air.
Misconception: Mirrors create a second you inside the wall. Fact: The mirror simply redirects light rays into your eyes.

visual_scenes.title: Straight Laser Beam & Mirror Bounce (Reflection)
visual_scenes.description: A sharp golden light ray strikes a polished silver flat mirror and bounces cleanly off at the exact same angle.
visual_scenes.caption: Step 1: Reflection! Light bounces off a mirror like a rubber ball!

visual_scenes.title: Bending Ray in Water (Refraction)
visual_scenes.description: A straight light beam enters a glass tank of blue water and noticeably bends downward at the water surface.
visual_scenes.caption: Step 2: Refraction! Light slows down in water and gently bends its path!

visual_scenes.title: Convex Lens Focuses Rays
visual_scenes.description: Parallel incoming beams pass through a clear convex lens and converge to a brilliant shining focal point (F).
visual_scenes.caption: Step 3: Convex Lens! The curved glass bends rays together to a sharp focus!

sign_glossary.description: Dominant hand starts pinched under chin and expands downward and outward into shining 5-handshape.
Dominant open hand held in front of face pivots slightly like checking one's reflection in a compact mirror.
Index finger points straight forward, then sharply bends 45 degrees downward at the second knuckle.
sign_glossary.movement: Straight trajectory then sharp angled bend

assessment_questions.question: What is the phenomenon called when light bounces off a shiny flat mirror?
assessment_questions.hint: Like looking at yourself in the mirror.

assessment_questions.question: Why does a straight pencil look bent when placed in a glass of water?
assessment_questions.expected_answer: Refraction bends the light as it enters water
options: Refraction bends the light as it enters water
The water broke the wooden pencil in half
The pencil melted inside the glass
Mirrors inside the glass play tricks
assessment_questions.hint: Light slows down and bends when changing media.
